quizName: Hardest Questions in New hampshire Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding decisions. What does "SEE" stand for?
questions.explanation: Good riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions. SEE means Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: To get the most protection from a helmet, choose one that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state safety standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: Turn signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are not very important since motorcycles are small.
Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Should not be used if other vehicles are far away.
Are harder to use than on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are at risk. Always use your turn signals to let other drivers know your plans. Use them every time you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, you should:
questions.explanation: When riding, tuck in your shoelaces securely. Loose laces can catch on your motorcycle.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a motorcycle crash is to:

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the single best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can be seen better by:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing with reflective materials so other drivers can see you. Keep your headlight on at all times. Use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should constantly look ahead for:
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for changing traffic, road hazards, and escape routes. Be ready to react to anything that changes.

questions.question: For the best protection, boots or shoes should:

options.text: Have long laces that are not tucked in.
Cover the ankle and give support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and give support.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Keep heels low so they won't catch on things. Tuck in long laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Your body can only get rid of alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, ideally made of leather, when riding. In hot weather, a leather jacket can help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are made to keep you cool even in heat.

questions.question: Wet surfaces can make it hard to control a motorcycle. Which surface is slippery?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Ride carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope to wake up.
Get off the road and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, rest every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: Riding gloves are often made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: For maximum protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: Use a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for maximum protection.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves when riding.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Protective clothing includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure, you should:

options.text: Look at the tire with your eyes.
Compare it to another tire's height.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire can look fine even when under-inflated, so looking is not enough.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious damage.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers keep you awake but do not lower your blood alcohol or make you sober.

questions.question: Use a turn signal:
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chances of being in an accident?

options.text: Try to blend in and not be noticed by other drivers.
Use turn signals only when driving at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Follow the vehicle ahead of you very closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake lights, and proper lane position to show your intentions. Keep safe distance from other vehicles, watch the road 12 seconds ahead, and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots that cover the ankles offer the best protection for motorcycle riders. High-top boots or heavy shoes work well. If your boots have long laces, tie them securely before riding.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It contains the motorcycle's specs, how to operate it, and maintenance schedules.

questions.question: Which surface provides the best traction for a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce traction for motorcycle tires. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates in roads are more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It can greatly reduce head injury severity.
It makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can greatly reduce head injury severity.
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet does not restrict your side vision.
